dedupe_keys.name: rapid flood and damage mapping using synthetic aperture radar in response to typhoon hagibis japan

description: Rapid flood and damage mapping using synthetic aperture radar in response to Typhoon Hagibis, Japan is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Cheryl W. J. Tay et al. During the aftermath of Typhoon Hagibis, we made flood and damage proxy maps, rapidly derived from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data using change detection approaches. The maps have large spatial coverage over the Tokyo, Fukushima, Ibaraki, Iwate, and Nagano prefectures of Japan. Coverage: national (JP); published in 2020. Formats: GeoTIFF, Shapefile, Image, KML. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC BY 4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
